title: Rigveda 10.155: Against a witch
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.155: Against a witch: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.155 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to against a witch. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 137v-138r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.155.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 137v
translation.original_text:
1arā̍yi̱ kāṇe̱ vika̍ṭe gi̱riṁ ga̍ccha sadānve | śi̱rimbi̍ṭhasya̱ satva̍bhi̱s tebhi̍ṣ ṭvā cātayāmasi ||
2ca̱tto i̱taś ca̱ttāmuta̱ḥ sarvā̍ bhrū̱ṇāny ā̱ruṣī̍ | a̱rā̱yya̍m brahmaṇas pate̱ tīkṣṇa̍śṛṇgodṛ̱ṣann i̍hi ||
3a̱do yad dāru̱ plava̍te̱ sindho̍ḥ pā̱re a̍pūru̱ṣam | tad ā ra̍bhasva durhaṇo̱ tena̍ gaccha parasta̱ram ||
translation.text:
1ARAYI, one-eyed limping hag, fly, ever-screeching, to the hill. We frighten thee away with these, the heroes of Ṣirimbiṭha.
2Scared from this place and that is she, destroyer of each germ unborn. Go, sharp-horned Brahmaṇaspati and drive Arayi far away.
3Yon log that floats without a man to guide it on the river's edge,– Seize it, thou thing with hideous jaws, and go thou far away thereon.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 137v (OPenn image 137, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.154.4 ‹pitṝn tapasvato yama tām̐ś›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 138r, begins in RV 10.155.4 ‹-budbudayāśavaḥ›. Verses 10.155.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.155.4-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 138r
translation.original_text:
4yad dha̱ prācī̱r aja̍ga̱ntoro̍ maṇḍūradhāṇikīḥ | ha̱tā indra̍sya̱ śatra̍va̱ḥ sarve̍ budbu̱dayā̍śavaḥ ||
5parī̱me gām a̍neṣata̱ pary a̱gnim a̍hṛṣata | de̱veṣv a̍krata̱ śrava̱ḥ ka i̱mām̐ ā da̍dharṣati ||
translation.text:
4When, foul with secret stain and spot, ye hastened onward to the breast, All Indra's enemies were slain and passed away like froth and foam.
5These men have led about the cow, have duly carried Agni round, And raised their glory tg the Gods. Who will attack them with success?
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 138r (OPenn image 137, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.155.4 ‹-budbudayāśavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 138v, begins in RV 10.157.2 ‹yajñaṁ ca nas tanvaṁ›. Verses 10.155.4-5 end on this page; 10.155.4 begins on fol. 137v.
